chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) about the Muṭamattiʿ (one performing Hajj al-Tamattuʿ) if he is an elderly man or a woman who fears menstruation, does he hasten the Tawaf of Hajj before coming to Minā? He said, 'Yes, whoever is in such a state, he hastens it.'
As for the Mufrid (one performing Hajj al-Qirān or Hajj al-Ifrād), it is permissible for him to advance the Tawaf before coming to Minā and ʿArafāt; this was narrated.

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: One performing Hajj al-Tamattuʿ (combining ʿUmrah and Hajj)
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: ʿArafāt, the plain where the standing (wuqūf) takes place

ai.seo_question: When must a pilgrim perform the Tawaf of Hajj if they have an excuse for delay?
ai.summary: Reported by Imam al-Rida (AS) via the chain of Saffan ibn Yahya, this hadith clarifies the flexibility in performing Tawaf al-Hajj for those with valid excuses, such as the elderly or women fearing menstruation, allowing them to hasten it before departing Minā. It further distinguishes the Mufrid, who may perform this Tawaf even before reaching Minā and ʿArafāt, highlighting the Shia juristic emphasis on ease (yusr) and removing hardship in ritual obligations.
